analysis:
The only change in this PR is a one-line docs edit to docs/reference/configuration.md (line 685). It changes the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE_SSD_INCREMENTAL_CHECKPOINTS row from 'Not forwarded to LaunchAgents' to 'Forwarded to the launchd provider job'. The two supplied head units (lines 1-485 of the file) do not include line 685, so that row is visible only in the patch excerpt. I reviewed the supplied units and found nothing security-relevant in the unchanged context.

Security relevance: the variable gates delta writes of recurrent complete checkpoints in the encrypted SSD prefix cache (T-041, A-001). It can only disable the feature (negative values) and defaults to on. If the documentation matches a corresponding code change in LaunchAgent.passthroughEnvironment, a daemon would honor an operator's rollback instead of always using the default. That does not weaken the existing T-041 controls: DBK3 AES-GCM, HMAC-keyed lookup tags, the 30-minute TTL, salt scoping and the DARKBLOOM_PREFIX_CACHE kill switch are unchanged by this PR.

The supplied evidence does not show the LaunchAgent.swift passthrough change, so I cannot confirm that code and docs agree. Passthrough is an allowlist of env keys the operator controls. The operator is already in the trust model as ADV-001, who has full local access (TB-003). Forwarding one disable-only boolean adds no new attack surface I can identify.

Remaining integration question: whether the code allowlist actually includes the key, since a doc/code mismatch would be a documentation-drift issue rather than a vulnerability. The delta checkpoint format in ssd-kv-cache.md is not supplied, so I could not check whether delta writes add any new prompt-derived plaintext metadata. T-041 forbids such metadata; this PR does not change the code that would introduce it.
